'''Prof. (emeritus) David Avnir''' ({{langx|he|דוד אבניר}}; born 12 June 1947; [[St. Ottilien Archabbey|St. Ottilien]], Germany) is an Israeli Professor of chemistry at the Institute of Chemistry, [[The Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].

His scientific activities include [[sol-gel]] materials, molecularly doped metals, [[Chirality (chemistry)|chirality]] and [[symmetry]] in experiments and theory. Earlier interests included [[fractals]] in [[chemistry]] and far-from-equilibrium phenomena. Current interests include also astrochemistry and geochemistry. He has authored and co-authored 420 papers (2025), many of which are highly cited, with an [[h-index]] of 87 and over 42,000 citations.<ref>{{GoogleScholar|ecGssEwAAAAJ}}</ref> Co-founder of the International Sol-Gel Society and its first chairman of the board. A "Highly Ranked Scholar - Lifetime" (in the top 0.05% of all scholars worldwide) according to the most recent (2024) ScholarGPS rankings.<ref>https://scholargps.com/scholars/10716960043646/david-avnir</ref> Awarded the Israel Chemical Society Gold Medal in 2024.

==Early life and family==

David Avnir was born in 1947 in a Displaced Persons hospital at the Benedictine archabbey of [[St. Ottilien Archabbey|St. Ottilien]], Germany.<ref>Photographs of Michaela Avnir, nee Steingarten, and her son David (born on June 12, 1947) in St. Ottilien http://dphospital-ottilien.org/babies/</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SgxYlv7vsIU |title=Die Kinder der Stunde Null - Sankt Ottilien, München, Jerusalem {{!}} ARD-alpha Doku |date=2020-05-10 |last=Berk TV |access-date=2025-05-21 |via=YouTube}}</ref> In 1949 he immigrated to Israel and lived in [[Jerusalem]] for all of his childhood and later on for most of his adult life. Married to Dr. Yehudit Avnir (emeritus) of The Paul Baerwald School of Social Work and Social Welfare, The Hebrew University of Jerusalem. They have two children and 4 grandchildren.

==Education==
Prof. Avnir received his BSc., MSc (Prof. Israel Agranat), and PhD. (Prof. Jochanan Blum) in chemistry from The Hebrew University of Jerusalem during the years 1969–1977. His post-doctoral studies were with Prof. Paul de Mayo, in the [[University of Western Ontario]], Canada, and with Prof. H. Morrison, at [[Purdue University]], United States, during the years 1978–1979.

==Academic positions==
* Senior Chemist, [[Teva Pharmaceutical Industries]], (1979–1980)

All of the following positions, at The Hebrew University of Jerusalem:

* Lecturer, Institute of Chemistry, (1980–1983)
* Senior Lecturer, Institute of Chemistry, (1983–1985)
* Associate Professor, Institute of Chemistry, (1985–1988)
* Full Professor, Institute of Chemistry, (1988–2016)
* Professor Emeritus, Institute of Chemistry, (2016–present)
* Chairman, School of Chemistry, (1991–1994)
* Head of the Institute of Chemistry, (2007–2010)
* Head of the Graduate Authority in the Experimental Sciences, (2011–2015)

==Founding activities==
* Founder and Editor-in-Chief, Heterogeneous Chemistry Reviews.<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/journal/1234-985X_Heterogeneous_Chemistry_Reviews Heterogeneous Chemistry Reviews]</ref> (1992–1997)
* Co-founder of Sol-Gel, Inc.<ref>{{Cite web |last=lsc-webmaster |date=2023-10-03 |title=Advancing Dermatological Innovation {{!}} Sol-Gel Technologies |url=https://www.sol-gel.com/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=www.sol-gel.com |language=en-US}}</ref> (1997)
* Co-Founder and chairman of the board, The International Sol-Gel Society.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-06-09 |title=International Sol-Gel Society |url=https://www.isgs.org/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |language=en-US}}</ref> (2003–2008)
* Scientific advisor and co-founder (2014) of the International Institute for "Solution Chemistry of Advanced Materials and Technologies" (SCAMT)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Home {{!}} SCAMT |url=https://scamt.ifmo.ru/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=scamt.ifmo.ru}}</ref> at [[ITMO University]], [[Saint Petersburg]], Russia.

==Research==

===Sol-gel materials===

The sol-gel methodology allows the preparation of [[glasses]] and [[ceramics]] at [[room temperature]]. Avnir's conceptual idea has been to use this low-temperature polymerization process for the incorporation of organic and bioorganic molecules within [[ceramic materials]]. Traditionally this has been impossible for [[glasses]] and [[ceramics]], because of the very high temperatures employed by these technologies. Following this general concept, the properties of ceramic materials could be altered to create a very wide range of previously unknown materials, by the ability to dope of [[glasses]] and [[ceramics]] with practically any of the ~40&nbsp;million organic and bioorganic molecules known today. The many useful applications include materials for optics, reactive materials, bioactive materials, [[catalysts]], [[sensors]] and [[functional aerogels]].<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/j150668a042 | title=The nature of the silica cage as reflected by spectral changes and enhanced photostability of trapped Rhodamine 6G | date=1984 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | last2=Levy | first2=David | last3=Reisfeld | first3=Renata | journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry | volume=88 | issue=24 | pages=5956–5959 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/cm00046a008 | title=Enzymes and Other Proteins Entrapped in Sol-Gel Materials | date=1994 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | last2=Braun | first2=Sergei | last3=Lev | first3=Ovadia | last4=Ottolenghi | first4=Michael | journal=Chemistry of Materials | volume=6 | issue=10 | pages=1605–1614 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1016/j.matlet.2007.03.046 | title=Biochemically active sol-gel glasses: The trapping of enzymes | date=2007 | last1=Braun | first1=Sergei | last2=Rappoport | first2=Sara | last3=Zusman | first3=Rivka | last4=Avnir | first4=David | last5=Ottolenghi | first5=Michael | journal=Materials Letters | volume=61 | issue=14–15 | pages=2843–2846 | bibcode=2007MatL...61.2843B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/ar00056a002 | title=Organic Chemistry within Ceramic Matrixes: Doped Sol-Gel Materials | date=1995 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | journal=Accounts of Chemical Research | volume=28 | issue=8 | pages=328–334 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1002/1521-3773(20011001)40:19<3647::AID-ANIE3647>3.0.CO;2-A | title=Acids and Bases in One Pot while Avoiding Their Mutual Destruction We gratefully acknowledge support from the Israel Science Foundation (Grant 96-98-2) and from the Infrastructure (Tashtiot) Project of the Israel Ministry for Science, Arts and Sports; and from the German–Israeli Foundation for Scientific Research and Development (Grant No. I-530.045.05/97). | date=2001 | last1=Gelman | first1=Faina | last2=Blum | first2=Jochanan | last3=Avnir | first3=David | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | volume=40 | issue=19 | pages=3647–3649 | pmid=11592209 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1039/b512706h | title=Recent bio-applications of sol–gel materials | date=2006 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | last2=Coradin | first2=Thibaud | last3=Lev | first3=Ovadia | last4=Livage | first4=Jacques | journal=J. Mater. Chem. | volume=16 | issue=11 | pages=1013–1030 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1016/j.mattod.2019.09.021 | title=Entrapment of enzymes in silica aerogels | date=2020 | last1=Ganonyan | first1=Nir | last2=Benmelech | first2=Noam | last3=Bar | first3=Galit | last4=Gvishi | first4=Raz | last5=Avnir | first5=David | journal=Materials Today | volume=33 | pages=24–35 }}</ref>

===Molecularly doped metals===

The family of doped metals was unknown until discovered and developed by Avnir in 2002. The methodology enables the incorporation and entrapment of organic molecules, [[polymers]], [[bioactive molecules]], enzymes and nanoparticles within [[metals]], rendering a metal with unconventional properties such as acidity, luminescence, magnetism or bioactivity.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/cm011558o | title=Entrapment of Organic Molecules within Metals: Dyes in Silver | date=2002 | last1=Behar-Levy | first1=Hanna | last2=Avnir | first2=David | journal=Chemistry of Materials | volume=14 | issue=4 | pages=1736–1741 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/ar4001982 | title=Molecularly Doped Metals | date=2014 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | journal=Accounts of Chemical Research | volume=47 | issue=2 | pages=579–592 | pmid=24283194 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1002/cctc.201601386 | title=Catalyst@Metal Hybrids in a One-Pot Multistep Opposing Oxidation and Reduction Reaction Sequence | date=2017 | last1=Shapiro | first1=Leora | last2=Avnir | first2=David | journal=ChemCatChem | volume=9 | issue=5 | pages=816–823 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/acsnano.9b06021 | title=Metallic Conductive Luminescent Film | date=2019 | last1=He | first1=Jin | last2=Ji | first2=Botao | last3=Koley | first3=Somnath | last4=Banin | first4=Uri | last5=Avnir | first5=David | journal=ACS Nano | volume=13 | issue=9 | pages=10826–10834 | pmid=31487452 | bibcode=2019ACSNa..1310826H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1039/c9sc05419g | title=Enzymes in a golden cage | date=2020 | last1=Baruch-Shpigler | first1=Yael | last2=Avnir | first2=David | journal=Chemical Science | volume=11 | issue=15 | pages=3965–3977 | pmid=34122867 | pmc=8152684 }}</ref>

===Chirality and symmetry ===

The first focal point of this broad topic has been the formation of new chiral materials, that is, materials which can appear in both left- and right-handed forms.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/ar6000236 | title=The Induction of Chirality in Sol–Gel Materials | date=2007 | last1=Marx | first1=Sharon | last2=Avnir | first2=David | journal=Accounts of Chemical Research | volume=40 | issue=9 | pages=768–776 | pmid=17591744 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1002/adma.200601702 | title=Chirality Induction in Bulk Gold and Silver | date=2007 | last1=Behar-Levy | first1=H. | last2=Neumann | first2=O. | last3=Naaman | first3=R. | last4=Avnir | first4=D. | journal=Advanced Materials | volume=19 | issue=9 | pages=1207–1211 | bibcode=2007AdM....19.1207B }}</ref> The second, related focal point has been the quantification of geometric symmetry and chirality: Traditionally these have been treated in terms of "either-or", but not as continuous structural properties that can evolve gradually from zero to fully-blown.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/ja00106a053 | title=Continuous Symmetry Measures. 4. Chirality | date=1995 | last1=Zabrodsky | first1=Hagit | last2=Avnir | first2=David | journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society | volume=117 | issue=1 | pages=462–473 | bibcode=1995JAChS.117..462Z }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/jo200648h | title=Quantifying Asymmetry in Concerted Reactions: Solvents Effect on a Diels–Alder Cycloaddition | date=2011 | last1=Tuvi-Arad | first1=Inbal | last2=Avnir | first2=David | journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry | volume=76 | issue=12 | pages=4973–4979 | pmid=21574602 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1002/prot.24706 | title=The near-symmetry of proteins | date=2015 | last1=Bonjack-Shterengartz | first1=Maayan | last2=Avnir | first2=David | journal=Proteins: Structure, Function, and Bioinformatics | volume=83 | issue=4 | pages=722–734 | pmid=25354765 }}</ref> The chirality/symmetry studies went also beyond [[chemistry]], and have included computerized analysis of symmetry, studies of the bilateral symmetry of [[Lower Paleolithic]] hand axes,<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1006/jasc.1997.0265 | title=Quantitative Analysis of the Symmetry of Artefacts: Lower Paleolithic Handaxes | date=1998 | last1=Saragusti | first1=I. | last2=Sharon | first2=I. | last3=Katzenelson | first3=O. | last4=Avnir | first4=D. | journal=Journal of Archaeological Science | volume=25 | issue=8 | pages=817–825 | bibcode=1998JArSc..25..817S }}</ref> and chirality in architecture.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s00004-013-0144-x | title=On Left and Right: Chirality in Architecture | date=2013 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | last2=Huylebrouck | first2=Dirk | journal=Nexus Network Journal | volume=15 | pages=171–182 }}</ref>

===Fractals ===

An ongoing major challenge has been the quantitative treatment of complex and irregular geometries in the context of the chemistry of materials and surfaces. A comprehensive solution for that problem was proposed by Avnir and his colleague Peter Pfeifer, by adapting [[fractal]] geometry to this challenge.<ref>{{Cite journal |doi=10.1063/1.446211 |title=Chemistry in noninteger dimensions between two and three. II. Fractal surfaces of adsorbents |date=1983 |last1=Avnir |first1=David |last2=Farin |first2=Dina |last3=Pfeifer |first3=Peter |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |volume=79 |issue=7 |pages=3566–3571 |bibcode=1983JChPh..79.3566A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1021/j150668a042 | title=The nature of the silica cage as reflected by spectral changes and enhanced photostability of trapped Rhodamine 6G | date=1984 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | last2=Levy | first2=David | last3=Reisfeld | first3=Renata | journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry | volume=88 | issue=24 | pages=5956–5959 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1126/science.279.5347.39 | title=Is the Geometry of Nature Fractal? | date=1998 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | last2=Biham | first2=Ofer | last3=Lidar | first3=Daniel | last4=Malcai | first4=Ofer | journal=Science | volume=279 | issue=5347 | pages=39–40 | arxiv=cond-mat/9801038 }}</ref> Avnir's edited text-book ''The Fractal Approach to Heterogeneous Chemistry: Surfaces, Colloids, Polymers'' (Wiley, Chichester, 1992) became a major source in this field and was reprinted several times.<ref>Wiley, Chichester, ''The Fractal Approach to Heterogeneous Chemistry: Surfaces, Colloids, Polymers'', David Avnir (ed.), 1992</ref>

===Dissipative structures===

This early work focused on the origin of patterns and structures which form as a result of reactions that solutions of chemicals undergo. Dissipative structures, as such structures are called, have been found for a wide array of different reactions.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1038/307717a0 | title=Spatial structures generated by chemical reactions at interfaces | date=1984 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | last2=Kagan | first2=Michael | journal=Nature | volume=307 | issue=5953 | pages=717–720 | bibcode=1984Natur.307..717A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1063/1.166128 | title=The evolution of chemical patterns in reactive liquids, driven by hydrodynamic instabilities | date=1995 | last1=Avnir | first1=D. | last2=Kagan | first2=M. L. | journal=Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science | volume=5 | issue=3 | pages=589–601 | pmid=12780214 | bibcode=1995Chaos...5..589A }}</ref>

===Astrochemistry and geochemistry===

Recent activity includes also topics in astrochemistry and geochemistry, particularly chirality aspects. Examples include an analysis of potential chirality indicators of extraterrestrial life;<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1016/j.newar.2020.101596 | title=Critical review of chirality indicators of extraterrestrial life | date=2021 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | journal=New Astronomy Reviews | volume=92 | article-number=101596 | bibcode=2021NewAR..9201596A | doi-access=free }}</ref> a detailed analysis of the correlation between aqueous alteration of meteorites and the enantiomeric excess of amino acids found in them;<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.3389/fspas.2024.1427260 | doi-access=free | title=On the correlation between the enantiomeric excess of L-isovaline and the level of aqueous alteration in carbonaceous meteorites | date=2024 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | journal=Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences | volume=11 | article-number=1427260 | bibcode=2024FrASS..1127260A }}</ref> and a comprehensive review of chiral minerals.<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.3390/min14100995 | doi-access=free | title=Chiral Minerals | date=2024 | last1=Avnir | first1=David | journal=Minerals | volume=14 | issue=10 | page=995 | bibcode=2024Mine...14..995A }}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==

Kaye Award for Applied Research (1998), The First Mehrotra Foundation Lecture (1998), Award Lecture of the Div. of Colloid and Surface Chem. of the [[Chemical Society of Japan]], (1998), The Kolthoff Award of the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]], (2004), The Benjamin H. Birstein Chair in Chemistry (2007),<ref>[https://chemistry.huji.ac.il/personal/emeriti The Benjamin H. Birstein Chair in Chemistry]</ref> Special issue of [[Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology]], honoring Prof. Avnir (2009),<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10971-009-1894-5 | doi=10.1007/s10971-009-1894-5 | title=David Avnir scientific achievements in the field of sol–gel materials | date=2009 | last1=Reisfeld | first1=Renata | journal=Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology | volume=50 | issue=2 | pages=127–129 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> Member of the [[Academia Europaea]] (2009),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Avnir_David|title=David Avnir|publisher=The Academy of Europe|accessdate=6 May 2020}}</ref> The Israel Chemical Society Prize (2011),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.isgs.org/community/prof-david-avnir/|title=Prof. David Avnir, awarded by the Israel Chemical Society Prize|date=21 September 2018|accessdate=6 May 2020}}</ref> Life-time Achievement Award of the International Sol-Gel Society (2013),<ref>{{cite journal|title=The 2013 Life Time Achievement Award of the International Sol–Gel Society awarded to Prof. David Avnir, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel|journal=Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology|volume=70|issue=2|pages=162–163|year=2014|doi=10.1007/s10971-014-3358-9|s2cid=195233426 |issn=0928-0707|eissn=1573-4846|oclc=704441918}}</ref> A collection of articles themed on "Hybrid Materials" dedicated to D. Avnir: Nanoscale, (2014), Fellow of the International Sol-Gel Society (2018), Distinguished Scientist, The [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (2018),<ref>{{cite news|url=https://chemistry.huji.ac.il/news/congratulations-david-avnir-being-elected-distinguished-scientist-2018-chinese|title=Prof. David Avnir is elected as a Distinguished Scientist by the Chinese Academy of Sciences|date=29 January 2018|accessdate=6 May 2020}}</ref> Israel Chemical Society Gold Medal (2024).
